scenario: The real publishAdminVideo use case publishes a ready synthetic SELF_HLS video through PostgreSQL.
The real enqueuePublishedVideoAnnouncement writes the durable NEW_VIDEO_FANOUT job in the publication transaction.
The post-commit announcePublishedVideo kick is verified as called, but replaced with a no-op to model losing the request process before it can start work.
A separate Node/tsx process starts the actual runNewVideoFanOutJobs worker and completes the persisted job.
An actual subscription receives exactly one NEW_VIDEO notification.
A repeated enqueue reopens the completed job; a second runner pass leaves the subscriber with exactly one notification.

vitest.command: DATABASE_URL=<disposable> DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED=<disposable> npx vitest run --config vitest.postgres.config.ts tests/postgres/published-video-notification-restart.pg.test.ts

scope_limits: The request-side publish use case runs in the Vitest process and its post-commit kick is replaced with a no-op; the HTTP server process is not killed after COMMIT.
The recovery worker is a fresh OS process; the actual scheduled cron HTTP endpoint was not called after restart.
HLS asset and active route are synthetic; no external R2/S3 provider or independent review was involved.
K23-T1/T2 and R05 remain partial until the HTTP crash/cron acceptance and remaining provider/review boundaries are verified.
